observations.summary: The chapter explicitly complements Chapter 4 by controlling apparent length rather than width.
The problem is real but narrow: a member can keep its identity while its projected length changes radically in depth.
Joint-as-pivot/member-as-radius adds a usable endpoint-reach diagnostic for invented foreshortening.
The plates use arcs as temporary tracking devices across multiple arm and leg positions; they are not presented as finished-image features.
Hogarth himself says ellipse dependence can become cumbersome; the triangle and part-to-part body checks are simplifications rather than a new figure foundation.
Teacher routing: preserve the range-of-motion/anatomy sanity-check value, but avoid multiplying redundant geometry cards.

rationale: The chapter appears mostly reinforcing, but the pivot/radius endpoint-reach idea is a concrete diagnostic delta worth a full unit read and targeted extraction.
